title: Tiered cooldown signal smoother and staged failover policy
creator: Arielle Mendoza
description: Replace brittle threshold-only fallback triggers with a tiered cooldown controller that smooths noisy signals and performs staged failovers (model-variant -> tier -> region). Focus is on reducing unnecessary fallback churn during transient spikes while ensuring fast protective action during real overloads (429 storms, timeouts, elevated 5xx).
background: Recent incidents showed repeated oscillation between primary model and fallback variants when short 429 bursts coincided with autoscaling lag. Existing trip-score thresholds react too quickly to single-window spikes and don't take downstream queueing into account. This ticket designs and implements a controller that uses smoothed signals, phase-aware circuit states, and a staged engagement plan to improve availability and cost predictability.
goals: Reduce fallback churn by >= 60% for transient 429 spikes in canary region
Ensure median remediation latency under 2s for persistent overload conditions
Provide per-tenant probation and decay so tenants with intermittent spikes are not permanently degraded
Expose observability and runbooks so SRE/Support can understand fallback actions and revert quickly
non_goals: Replace autoscaling — autoscaler remains the primary capacity fix
Major runtime kernel changes — controller will operate at routing layer and use existing runtime signals
design_summary: We will implement a phase-aware controller with four states: NORMAL, PROBATION, DEGRADED, and FALLBACK. Signals ingested: 429 rate, p95 latency, 5xx rate, request queue length, and model health pings. Each signal is first smoothed using an EWMA with configurable alpha per signal (defaults: 0.2 for latency, 0.15 for error rates, 0.3 for queue length). A composite risk score is computed as a weighted sum of normalized smoothed signals. Thresholds for state transitions are asymmetric and include hysteresis windows. On first exceedance controller enters PROBATION (short cool-off window) to confirm persistence; if sustained, it escalates to DEGRADED and engages a staged failover: 1) switch a subset of traffic to a cheaper quantized variant; 2) expand to tier-level fallback (lower tier capacity); 3) region-level handoff if regional capacity metrics indicate overload. Each engagement has a probation timer and a decay schedule so mitigations automatically retract after stability is observed. Circuit breaker counts are tracked per-tenant and per-route to avoid global collateral. Controller publishes events to tracing and an events topic for audit and console timeline.
key_implementation_details: Signal preprocessing: use existing router metrics pipeline (metrics-agent -> tsdb) and add 200ms streaming window for near-realtime EWMA updates
Composite risk score normalization: map each smoothed metric to 0..1 using sliding baselines (historic 7d p50/p95) to avoid static thresholds
Phase durations: PROBATION=10s, DEGRADED=60s, FALLBACK cooldown=5m default (configurable per-customer)
Per-tenant hysteresis: maintain decay tokens that reduce required exceedance by 50% after repeated safe runs over 30m
Engagement actions: model-variant route rewrite at router proxy, tier shift via route priority change, region handoff via smart-routing table update
Telemetry: emit fallback events with fields: reason, score, actions_taken, affected_routes, tenant_id, before_state, after_state, timestamp
Safety: allow explicit ignore lists and emergency-disable at org level; integrate with existing rollout/fallback policies in Console
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for EWMA smoothing and composite score computation
Chaos job that simulates 429 spikes demonstrates >=60% reduction in flip-flop compared to baseline
Dashboard tiles showing composite score, per-tenant circuit counts, and mitigation timelines in Console
Runbook created with steps to inspect events topic, rollback staged failover, and add tenant-specific overrides
Canary rollout to region-us-west-2 with traffic-slice 1% and no customer-impact alerts for 72h

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives causing unnecessary costlier fallbacks. Mitigation: probation window + sliding baselines + staged engagement to prefer cheap model-variant first.

Risk: delayed reaction to genuine overloads. Mitigation: include queue length and p95 latency so queueing signals accelerate escalation; short-circuit path for extreme 5xx burst (>30% 5xx in 5s) to immediate FALLBACK.
Risk: telemetry volume growth. Mitigation: sample events for high-throughput tenants and keep full trace only for probations and escalations.

Risk: interactions with Dedicated autoscaling. Mitigation: consult Dedicated infra and add compatibility layer that honors reserved capacity flags and avoids region-level handoff when reserved capacity limits apply.

decisions: Use EWMA for smoothing (configurable alpha) instead of fixed sliding-window counts to better handle variable traffic patterns
Default staged engagement order: model-variant -> tier -> region. This order minimizes cost and scope of change.
Expose per-tenant config: cooldown durations and disabled stages. Default conservative settings used for self-serve customers and stricter for enterprise by request.
